Sep core capital goods orders, excluding defense and air transportation, rose +1.2%, stronger than market expectations of +0.8%.

He also called for strengthening ties with neighboring countries after top officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye met on Monday in Tehran. On the US side, President Trump told Fox News on Sunday that it's "getting to be decision time" on whether he will make a deal with Iran or "finish it off." The US is building up military forces in the Middle East into November and is evacuating non-essential embassy personnel in the Gulf region, fueling speculation that the US might launch a new military attack on Iran after next Tuesday's (Nov 3) US election.

wall street stock market flag new york trading equity -Shutterstock

US equity futures were trending higher on Tuesday as traders await the latest batch of corporate earnings.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 were up 0.3% in premarket activity, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.2%. Wall Street finished the previous trading session up, with the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 snapping a two-day losing streak.

Coca-Cola (KO), Boeing (BA), Corning (GLW), HCA Healthcare (HCA), Johnson Controls International (JCI), United Parcel Service (UPS), Sherwin-Williams (SHW), Hilton Worldwide (HLT), Royal Caribbean Cruises (RCL), PayPal (PYPL) and Centene (CNC) report their latest financial results before the bell, among others.

Payments giant Visa (V), Waste Management (WM), Robinhood Markets (HOOD) and NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) post their earnings after the markets close.

S&P 500 third-quarter profit momentum slowed this week as a pullback in technology-sector earnings tempered otherwise broad-based gains across all market sectors, Oppenheimer Asset Management said Monday in a report. So far, 122 companies, or 24% of the index, have reported results, with earnings growth slowing to 38% from about 47% a week earlier, according to the brokerage.

The Federal Reserve's monetary policy committee is set to kick off its meeting on interest rates today, with a decision due Wednesday. The probability of the central bank leaving its benchmark lending rate unchanged currently stands at 90%, with the remaining odds in favor of a quarter-percentage-point increase, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"Despite a notable pickup in both consumer and producer prices in the latest September report, a number of Fed officials have urged the (Federal Open Market Committee) to take a more cautious and patient approach to any additional rate hikes," Stifel Economics Chief Economist Lindsey Piegza said in a Monday note emailed to MT Newswires. "While the majority of officials still support some further policy firming, most also appear to support a slow or more tepid pace of adjustments."

Treasury yields were mixed early Tuesday, with the two-year ticking down 1 basis point to 4.71% while the 10-year rate up 0.2 basis points to 4.99%.

Tuesday's economic calendar includes the durable goods orders report for September at 8:30 am ET, followed by the Case-Shiller Home Price Index and the Federal Housing Finance Agency House Price Index, both for August, at 9 am.

The consumer confidence report and the Richmond Fed manufacturing index, both for October, are out at 10 am, along with last month's new home sales report.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil inclined 0.2% to $102 a barrel, while Brent inched 0.1% higher to $115.92 a barrel.

Iran's officials met with representatives from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey on Monday, with Riyadh saying the discussions were aimed at keeping diplomatic channels open and preventing further escalation in hostilities, CNBC reported.

Shares of Celestica (CLS) surged 17% pre-bell as the company reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results. Whirlpool (WHR) dropped 9.3% after the company said it now expects to report a loss for 2026, compared with previous projections for a profit.

Meta Platforms (META) decreased 0.4% after Nvidia (NVDA) said it will expand its partnership with the Facebook parent to develop its Muse family of artificial intelligence models and invest $3 billion in the company's equity offering.

Spot gold dipped 0.7% to $4,011 per troy ounce, while bitcoin was off 0.6% to $79,432.

U.S. stock futures were up in premarket trading ahead of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting, following Monday's Wall Street gains.

Oil reversed early losses, with Brent crude futures rising above $116 a barrel and WTI crude futures topping $102 amid shifting U.S.-Iran peace hopes.

SoFi and PayPal shares fell ahead of their results, while Broadcom and Uber stocks edged higher.

U.S. stock futures rose early on Tuesday after Wall Street closed higher in the previous session, lifted by artificial-intelligence optimism following Anthropic's filing for an initial public offering (IPO).

As of 5.30 a.m. ET, Nasdaq 100 futures were up 0.11%, while Dow futures rose 0.18% and S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%.

Earlier on Monday, the S&P 500 ended 0.7% higher, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.3%, and the Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, advanced 0.4%.

Investors are now turning their attention to a fresh batch of corporate earnings and the start of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting.

Oil Prices Rebound After Early Losses

Oil prices initially fell on Tuesday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war raised hopes of easing tensions across the wider region, where the conflict has also involved Tehran-backed Houthis supporting Saudi Arabia.

However, prices later pared their losses and moved into positive territory. By around 5.30 a.m. ET, Brent crude futures had risen 0.47% to $116.36 a barrel, while WTI crude futures gained 0.51% to $102.27 a barrel.

The Tech Radar

Nvidia (NVDA): The company announced a $3 billion investment in Meta Platforms' (META) equity offering and a partnership to improve Meta's Muse AI agentic platform. Meta announced a $97.5 billion equity offering on Monday. Later in the day, it said it had sold $12.5 billion in preferred shares at $50 apiece and $25 billion in common stock at $625 per share. META shares traded 0.15% higher in early premarket trading.

SK Hynix (SKHY): South Korean newspaper Dong-A Ilbo reported that the memory chipmaker was considering a special dividend of around 16 trillion won ($12 billion). The report came ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings announcement on Wednesday.

Celestica (CLS): Shares of the company jumped nearly 17% in early premarket trading on Tuesday after the data center infrastructure firm posted better-than-expected third-quarter results and signaled strong demand for AI-related infrastructure. Qualcomm Just Dropped 13% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©@Tim Girard from Tim Girard's Images via Canva; @Soulful Pizza from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Qualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) stock dropped 13% in the month through October 22, with a September 28 semiconductor selloff accounting for more than half the decline.

Arm Holdings (ARM:NASDAQ) fell 37% over the same period, compared with the Nasdaq 100's 6% decline, highlighting broader semiconductor weakness.

Apple (AAPL:NASDAQ) remains a major headwind, with Qualcomm expecting Apple-related revenue to decline approximately 50% sequentially in the December quarter.

Qualcomm looks better suited for holding than aggressively buying, trading near 19x forward earnings against its five-year average of 14x.

What Happened?

Qualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) stock declined 13% over the past month through October 22, closing near $173 as investors weighed weaker smartphone demand, Apple-related revenue losses, and broader semiconductor volatility.

The biggest setback came on September 28, when Qualcomm shares dropped 7% amid inflation concerns, rising Treasury yields, and technology-sector selling pressure.

Arm Holdings (ARM:NASDAQ) fell nearly 9% that session. Over the full month, Arm lost 37%, compared with Qualcomm's 13% decline and the Nasdaq 100's 6% drop, highlighting semiconductor stocks' underperformance.

The selloff followed positive developments, including Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit, an Apple patent-license renewal, and an Amazon Web Services partnership. However, those announcements failed to offset concerns about handset demand.

Qualcomm also announced a multi-year patent cross-license agreement with Huawei on October 5, covering AI, 5G, computing, and networking technologies.

On October 13, a Delaware jury found that Arm breached its licensing agreement with Qualcomm, awarding $2 in nominal damages while leaving significant royalty questions unresolved.

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that CEO Cristiano Amon outlined a global "performance-focused reduction" in staffing, with employee notifications beginning in November.

Despite these developments, Qualcomm's biggest challenge remains smartphones.

Management expects handset-market weakness to pressure Android chip revenue, while Apple-related revenue could decline approximately 50% from the September quarter to the December quarter.

Still, diversification offers encouragement. Non-handset revenue increased 28% last quarter, while automotive revenue reached a record $1.6 billion.

Qualcomm also targets $5 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2027 and more than $15 billion by fiscal 2029, potentially creating a meaningful growth engine beyond smartphones.

Robinhood Just Dropped 11% in a Week. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©Billion Photos and Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Robinhood stock fell 11.6% in the five trading sessions through October 19, more than three times the Nasdaq 100's 3.7% decline.

Wolfe Research downgraded Robinhood to Peer Perform, while Wells Fargo reduced its price target to $120.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to increase from $2.34 in 2025 to $3.43 in 2027, suggesting substantial earnings growth remains possible.

Robinhood's October 27 earnings report could determine whether the selloff creates a buying opportunity or signals further downside.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD:NASDAQ) stock dropped 11.6% in the five trading sessions through October 19, compared with a 3.7% decline in the Nasdaq 100.

Shares closed at $96.52 that Monday, approximately 36% below their 52-week high. The question is whether Robinhood's growth prospects justify buying after the correction.

What Happened?

Robinhood fell 8.5% on October 14 after Wolfe Research downgraded the stock from Outperform to Peer Perform, arguing that much of the expected good news was already reflected in its valuation.

Wells Fargo also reduced its price target from $125 to $120 while maintaining an Equal Weight rating.

Broader weakness in financial and technology stocks added pressure. Robinhood rebounded 2.9% on October 15 before declining another 4.9% the following session. Over the month through October 22, Robinhood fell 22%, compared with declines of 16% for Coinbase (COIN:NASDAQ) and 14% for SoFi (SOFI:NASDAQ), showing that Robinhood faced greater selling pressure than its fintech peers.

The selloff reflects concern about how much investors should pay for Robinhood's future growth, rather than evidence of a sudden collapse in the business.

Is Robinhood Stock Undervalued After the Selloff?

Robinhood's forward P/E declined from approximately 43x at the end of 2025 to 33.4x on October 16, well below its October 2025 peak of 75.5x.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

However, the stock isn't necessarily cheap. Its multiple previously fell to approximately 28x in March, leaving room for additional valuation compression.

Meanwhile, analysts expect normalized EPS to increase from $2.34 in 2025 to $3.43 in 2027, representing approximately 47% cumulative growth.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)

Robinhood is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on October 27, with analysts expecting approximately $1.44 billion in revenue.

Event contracts generated $156 million in Q2, while cryptocurrency revenue totaled $100 million. These businesses, alongside net deposits, will be important indicators of whether Robinhood can maintain its growth.

title: FIGS Just Gained 49% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
detail:
FIGS Just Gained 49% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
Nikko Henson
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 1:15 AM MST 4 min read
^GSPC
^NDX
FIGS Just Gained 49% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More? ©Minerva Studio via Canva
Key Takeaways

FIGS stock climbed 48.9% in the month through October 19, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.6% gain.

Second-quarter revenue increased 28.8% to $196.6 million, prompting management to raise its full-year growth outlook to about 20%.

Shares traded at approximately 55x forward earnings, while analysts expected normalized EPS growth of just 6% in 2027.

Holding looks more attractive than buying more ahead of November 5 earnings, given the stock's premium valuation.

FIGS (FIGS:NYSE) stock surged 48.9% in the month ended October 19, closing at $19.45 as investors rewarded the healthcare apparel company for its improving financial performance.

The rally significantly outpaced the broader market. The S&P 500 gained just 0.6% during the same period, while the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.4%.

Interestingly, FIGS released almost no company-specific news during the stretch. Strong earnings, rising expectations, and momentum appear to have fueled the gains.

The question now is whether those improving fundamentals justify its increasingly expensive valuation.

What's Driving FIGS Stock Higher?

FIGS experienced several sharp price movements, including a 12.4% gain on October 12, when trading volume reached approximately 11.3 million shares, nearly four times its usual level.

The rally followed an impressive second-quarter earnings report in August. Revenue increased 28.8% year over year to $196.6 million, marking the company's third consecutive quarter of growth exceeding 25%.

Diluted EPS reached $0.15, compared with analyst expectations of $0.07. Management raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to about 20%, from 14% to 16%, and expanded its share repurchase authorization by $100 million.

CEO Trina Spear highlighted the company's "strong, ongoing traction across the business," reflecting improvements across its operations.

Non-scrubwear revenue grew 40.3% to $35.4 million, while international revenue surged 67% to $37.9 million.

By comparison, Nike (NKE:NYSE) reported a 4% revenue decline in its fiscal first quarter of 2027. Although the companies serve different apparel markets, FIGS' stronger recent sales momentum stands out.

Profitability also improved. Gross margin reached 75.2%, up 820 basis points, although 780 basis points came from tariff refunds. Adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 18.6% from 12.9%, excluding the benefit of prior-year tariff refunds.

Those results explain why Wall Street has become more optimistic.

FIGS (FIGS): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)

Analysts expect normalized EPS of $0.36 in 2026, nearly double the $0.19 recorded in 2025.

title: Bitcoin and ETH Holders Could Face a Deeper Pullback, Ansem Warns
detail:
Bitcoin and ETH Holders Could Face a Deeper Pullback, Ansem Warns
Phil Haunhorst
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:38 AM MST 3 min read
BTC-USD
QQQ
ETH-USD
^NDX
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by BeInCrypto

Crypto trader Ansem has turned bearish on Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH). He warns that both assets broke their mid-timeframe trend and could slide faster below $82,000 and $2,400.

Ansem also says being bullish onchain has become a contrarian position. In his view, sentiment is the worst he has seen in roughly nine years, and Bitcoin and ETH holders could face a deeper pullback.

Why Ansem Turned Bearish on Bitcoin Now

Ansem bases his call largely on stock market technicals. In his view, AI momentum stocks printed a parabolic blow-off top, a steep final surge that often marks the end of a rally. A lower high and a broken trend followed.

Meanwhile, he says even the largest tech names are stalling at all-time highs. He adds that a recent breakout in the Invesco QQQ, a fund that tracks the Nasdaq 100, has turned into a failed move above prior highs.

Ansem. Source: X

He also questions where the next wave of AI revenue will come from. He argues that heavy spending on model training has yet to lift profits in a meaningful way, and he points to Meta's post-earnings selloff as an example.

Headline risk adds more pressure. The Federal Reserve announces its rate decision on October 28, in a packed Fed week that also brings major earnings reports.

Crypto analyst Benjamin Cowen has also laid out a bearish Q4 roadmap for Bitcoin.

Bitcoin Price Performance. Source: BeInCrypto
Can Onchain Builders Lift the Mood?

Still, Ansem is not bearish on Bitcoin over the longer term. He expects a pullback first and then a move higher.

The crypto trader also expects heavy volatility in both directions through the fourth quarter. Even so, he believes parts of the onchain market could still do well.

Ansem saves his sharpest criticism for Crypto Twitter itself. Traders complain about lower price ceilings on tokens, he says, while too few people build protocols that could change that.

Ansem. Source: X

His optimism on select tokens matches his August call, when Ansem predicted that Pump.fun's token could join crypto's top 10 by 2028.

For now, Ansem is bearish on Bitcoin but still sees room for some onchain projects. In his view, tokens will only break through lower price ceilings if builders put in the work to ship protocols worth owning.

Dell Stock Sinks 21% in a Week After Barclays Downgrade: Is the AI Rally Losing Steam? ©Lisa Fotios from Pexels and ispyfriend from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dell stock fell 21% over the five trading sessions ending October 19, significantly underperforming the Nasdaq 100.

Barclays downgraded Dell, questioning whether higher memory prices rather than stronger enterprise AI demand are driving revenue growth.

Dell reported $47 billion in quarterly revenue and a $95 billion AI backlog, although free cash flow declined 47%.

Dell traded near 16x forward earnings, making cash flow performance a key test of its valuation.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) shares fell 21% over the five trading sessions ending October 19, compared with a 3.7% decline in the Nasdaq 100.

The biggest drop came October 14, when Dell plunged 11.3% following a Barclays downgrade. AI server competitor Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) fell 19.7% over the same period, highlighting broader weakness across AI infrastructure stocks.

Higher interest rate expectations and concerns about AI hardware valuations added pressure. Despite the correction, Dell remained up approximately 262% in 2026 through October 19.

Why Barclays Is Questioning Dell's AI Growth

Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded Dell from Overweight to Equal Weight and lowered his price target from $603 to $574, citing valuation concerns and limited evidence of a meaningful AI spending inflection among enterprise customers.

The bank questioned how much of Dell's revenue growth comes from higher memory prices rather than stronger underlying demand.

If memory prices stabilize, revenue growth could slow even while AI server demand remains healthy.

Dell's fiscal second-quarter revenue increased 58% to $47 billion, while AI orders reached a record $60.9 billion and its backlog climbed to $95 billion.

Wall Street expects revenue of approximately $193 billion for the fiscal year ending January 2027 and $229 billion the following year.

Dell Technologies (DELL): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (years to January) (TIKR)
Dell's Next Major Test Is Cash Flow

Dell generated $986 million in free cash flow during its fiscal second quarter, down 47% year over year, as customer financing receivables absorbed $6.67 billion in cash.

Analysts expect approximately $12 billion in full-year free cash flow. With $4.10 billion generated in the first half, Dell would need roughly $7.9 billion in the second half to meet that estimate.

That makes cash conversion an important test as Dell works through its growing AI backlog.

Is Dell Stock Attractively Valued After the Selloff?

Dell's forward P/E declined from an August peak above 26x to around 16x as of October 16, but remained above its five-year average of approximately 12x.
